headline: Keys are on the wiki's Uninsurable Items list, so a key is NEVER recoverable via insurance in any mode. The only thing that protects a key is your secure container - and nearly every ordinary key and keycard is secure-container eligible. So insurance is not the differentiator people assume; durability, room contest and access blocks are.

one_liners.advice: Do Lightkeeper's Snatch to make the Lab access loop positive-yield, farm Reserve's three marked rooms instead of dorm 314 (same loot table, and the used keys barter into a 314 key at Jaeger LL3), and remember your insurance edge switches off entirely in The Lab, The Labyrinth and on Icebreaker — pouch the key, run a throwaway kit there, and save the insured loadout for Customs, Reserve, Interchange and Shoreline.

Stop buying anything with a guaranteed in-raid spawn (Knossos, Cardinal apartment key, the Terminal three, the Boreas cards, the residential unit keycard) and instead bring real gear, because an AI killer means a high chance of full insurance return everywhere except The Lab, The Labyrinth and Icebreaker — then run one map's whole key circuit per raid on the local client, with Object #11SR saved for last because entering it force-extracts you.

Spend nothing: bootstrap off free mechanical keys (Dorm guard desk, Dorm 110, Factory emergency exit, room 301) on the four maps Black Division do not roam — Customs, Reserve, Interchange, Factory — take Safecracker for -5 points because durability is your real cost with no insurance, prefer private exfils over rich rooms, and never burn a UHF RFID Reader on an #11SR or Green keycard craft because Lightkeeper cannot rebuild it before 7 December.

divergences.mechanic: The saferoom door "will lock itself after closing, and extract any PMC inside" — the extraction is forced, not optional — and the card is power-switch gated.
divergences.effect: Best in PvP Season, where insurance is disabled and a forced bank-out with a Weapon box (4x4), (6x3), (5x5) and modded M4A1s is the only way to keep anything, on a map Black Division do not roam. Good in PvP Zone as a one-button bail-out of a lost mall fight. Poor in PvE Zone, where it terminates the multi-room circuit that is the mode's entire advantage, so it must be the last stop of a raid or not run at all. Never craft it in Season: the recipe eats a UHF RFID Reader and an Object #21WS keycard at Intelligence Center 2.

divergences.mechanic: The whole cost is an audience cost — a map-wide power switch you must flip, a store-wide alarm 3 seconds after the door opens, and a second grate door to stand at afterwards.
divergences.effect: Best in PvE Zone, where no official source credits AI PMCs with flipping the switch or reacting to the alarm, so a four-stage advertisement becomes a four-stage errand and nobody is inside the gun store first — the catch being that you pay the power detour yourself every single raid. Poor in PvP Zone (the alarm is a free location ping) and poor in PvP Season for the same reason with no insurance behind the death. Note neither KIBA key has a trader or a price on the wiki, so there is no shopping trip — flea or in-raid only.

divergences.key: The Lab chain: TerraGroup Labs access keycard, keycard (Black), Cardinal apartment key
divergences.mechanic: Lightkeeper gates the UHF RFID Reader re-craft (task Snatch) and is inaccessible in Season; on seasonal characters Raiders on The Lab are replaced by Black Division and the transit out of The Lab is disabled.
divergences.effect: Good to best in PvP Zone and PvE Zone, where the reader loop is positive-yield — net +2 access cards per cycle at the cost of a VPX Flash Storage Module, an Advanced Electronic Materials textbook, a Secure Flash drive and an Intelligence folder, so not free and not a 40-minute farm — and where the Lab-to-Streets transit turns one card into the Kruglov's-safe-to-Cardinal-apartment chain. Poor to unavailable in Season, where every card burns a reader you cannot rebuild, the Lab is occupied by Black Division, and the transit that carried the chain out is gone.

divergences.key: Factory emergency exit key (and the escape-key class generally)
divergences.mechanic: Insurance is disabled only in PvP Season; in PvE the Insurance page states an AI killer gives "a high chance you'll get everything back". Keys themselves are uninsurable in every mode.
divergences.effect: Best in PvP Season: with no insurer, surviving is the only way to keep a kit, and two private Factory extractions plus the Customs ZB-013 door on two Black-Division-free maps is the cheapest survival tool available, renewable at Jaeger LL2 for ration-pack junk. Good in PvP Zone, where the same escape saves an insured kit you would otherwise wait 1-20 hours for. Poor in PvE Zone, where every killer is AI and returns are near-certain, making route time spent on an exfil the worst trade in the mode.

divergences.key: The Terminal set: Pier door key, Black Division keycard, Armory key
divergences.mechanic: Terminal returns your character state as it was before entering when you leave "by either dying or extracting" — nothing can be lost and nothing can be banked, in any mode. All three keys are guaranteed free in-raid spawns; the scarce item is the single-use access item, and the access routes are mutually exclusive story branches.
divergences.effect: Good in PvP Zone, the only mode where Prestige is documented, so Terminal converts into the ladder (Kruglov's RFID keycard for Prestige 4 and 5 is a story payout of The Ticket, not a Terminal drop; Prestige 6 requires completing The Ticket). Fine in PvP Season, where Terminal stays open via Prapor's letter at LL1 or the Reprogrammed RFID crafts halved by Handyman, and is the one location where having no insurance costs literally nothing. Poor in PvE Zone: Terminal forces BSG servers, there is no Prestige to feed, and zero-risk carry is redundant. The Armory key drops in every mode because the confiscated equipment cannot be extracted at all.

agnostic.why: Costs nothing (dead Scav in the two-story dorm shower), is secure-container and Key tool storable, and is the documented spawn room for the Dorm 314 marked key plus 104, 105, 108, 118, 204, 218, 303, 308, 315, the Trailer park portable cabin key and the Tarcone Director's office key. Every mode wants the Customs key set and this is the only door that hands it to you. Caveat: the wiki does not describe its spawn as guaranteed per raid.

agnostic.key: RB-VO / RB-BK / RB-PKPM marked keys (the Reserve set)
agnostic.why: One shared marked-room loot table, no mode-specific gating, and Reserve avoids the Season Black Division roam list. All three are mechanical (Safecracker-eligible in Season), all three are secure-container and Key tool storable so they ride together in any mode, and once used they barter at Jaeger LL3 into a Dorm 314 marked key. This is the marked-room money regardless of mode; dorm 314 is not.

agnostic.key: Health Resort west wing room 301 key
agnostic.why: Free spawn on a seat of the yellow bus by the collapsed tunnel, and one unlock plus one balcony hop reaches three graphics card spawns, multiple LEDX, a 5x5 weapon box and an SV-98 across rooms 301 and 304. Highest loot-per-unlock on Shoreline in every mode; Season only discounts it for the Black Division roam, and Handyman repays part of that by halving the crafts you feed with the haul.

Ref LL1 for 1x Lega Medal + 100x GP coin is the earliest hideout barter in any mode, and it is a guaranteed TerraGroup Labs keycard (Yellow) spawn behind one door in the eastern village. Woods carries no Black Division roam in Season, and Arena progression syncs one-way into all three profiles, so nothing about the barter is mode-locked.

You cannot skip it in any mode: it is a required location for both Provocation and Irresistible. Behind it are a Weapon box (4x4), (6x3) and (5x2), a SIG MPX and a HighCom Trooper TFO. Acquire one from bosses, Cultists, The Goons, rare valuables crates or any marked room rather than the flea, and do not feed it to the Object #11SR craft, which consumes both a 21WS and a UHF RFID Reader.

table.why_it_moves: Wiki verbatim: the door "will lock itself after closing, and extract any PMC inside" — so it is loot plus a forced raid end, which is a guaranteed bank-out when nothing is insured (Season, on a Black-Division-free map), a bail-out with your kit in PvP Zone, and a circuit-killer in PvE where the whole thesis is looting many rooms per raid.

The cost is entirely an audience cost — you flip a map-wide power switch, then an alarm rings across the mall 3 seconds after the door opens, then you stand at a second grate door; PvE deletes the audience (no official source credits AI PMCs with flipping power or hearing alarms), while Season adds the worst possible pairing of an alarm-marked stand with zero insurance.

Insurance is disabled only in PvP Season, so surviving is the only way to keep a kit and two private Factory exfils plus the Customs ZB-013 door become the cheapest survival insurance available; in PvE the Insurance page says an AI killer gives "a high chance you'll get everything back", so escape is worth least exactly where deaths are cheapest.

table.map: Streets of Tarkov (key spawns in The Lab R22 safe)
table.why_it_moves: The chain needs you to pull the free guaranteed key from Kruglov's safe and get it to Streets; on seasonal characters Raiders on The Lab are replaced by Black Division and the transit out of The Lab is disabled, breaking the chain at step one. PvP Zone and PvE differ only in that Streets forces BSG servers in PvE, so PvE loses its local-client safety net here.

The UHF RFID Reader re-craft is gated behind Lightkeeper's Snatch, and Lightkeeper is inaccessible in Season — so the card loop is positive-yield (net +2 cards per cycle, not free) in both Zone modes and strictly one-way in Season; PvE ranks highest because one consumed card covers a full multi-room Lab sweep instead of one contested room.

In PvE R22 is a deterministic pull that yields the guaranteed Cardinal apartment key; in PvP Zone the value is the downstream Blue Folders to Lightkeeper barter that only the two Zone modes can reach; in Season the Lab is Black-Division-occupied with no transit out and the Lightkeeper leg is closed outright.

A seasonal change routes Against the Conscience - Part 1 straight after Create a Distraction - Part 1 without the Arena quest Hold the Lead, which cannot be obtained in season — so Season is the only mode reaching this room's chain (ending at Between Two Fires / Decisions, Decisions) without Arena, and the room drops the loose GP coins the Theta barter wants.

Terminal restores character state on death *and* on extraction in every mode, so no key or loot is ever at risk or ever bankable; the residual value is progression, and Prestige is documented only for the PvP game mode. PvE additionally loses the local client (Terminal forces BSG servers) and has no Prestige ladder to feed.

Same Terminal reset rule, and the keycard is a guaranteed free spawn every raid in the seaport weapon box in all modes — so it is never the scarce item. Season keeps Terminal open via Prapor's letter (LL1) or the Reprogrammed RFID crafts (halved by Handyman); only the Lightkeeper route is closed.

Demoted in every mode: because the state reset applies to extracting too, the confiscated equipment cannot be taken out at all, so it is not a gear room in any economic sense — only a leg of the Mr. Kerman access branch, which is worth least in PvE where there is no Prestige and Terminal forces servers.

Identical marked-room loot table to Reserve's three rooms but the most camped door in human lobbies, and the wiki calls the key "completely rusted through, making it very fragile" — so Season's opt-in Safecracker (25% chance of no durability loss) is the only mode that cushions that, on a map Black Division do not roam; PvE simply removes the stairwell camper.

It is a guaranteed free spawn every raid, and a guarantee only becomes genuinely yours when nobody else is racing you; the lock sits in the west wing basement, the most contested building on Shoreline in both human modes, and Shoreline is a Black Division roam map in Season. Insurers return nothing from The Labyrinth in any mode.

Six large supply crates is minutes of standing still, which is the single variable PvE changes most (and Reserve is local-client eligible); Season keeps the map safe from Black Division but bulk crate loot is the worst fit for -20% sell payouts, 5% commission and a 7 December deletion date.

table.key: Kiba Arms inner grate door key
table.why_it_moves: Not an independent pick — it carries no power requirement and no alarm note of its own, so it is purely the outer door key's dependency; it inherits that key's mode profile and should never be bought first.

Season makes the hideout the money engine (no Found-in-Raid for zones, craft times halved, Crafting starts at 51) while making the UHF RFID Reader non-renewable, so the Intelligence folder and generator fuel behind this ten-second ground-floor door are the half of the keycard craft you can still control; in both Zone modes the reader is re-craftable so folder supply does not bind.

Armor Shortage is a confirmed Season 1 modifier and nothing is insured, so mannequins handing out Slicks and Trooper TFO are worth several times their Zone-mode value — and the key's Cultist Circle sacrifice is halved by Handyman; partly offset because Streets is one of the three Black Division roam maps.

Pure insurance arbitrage: a door that can hand you a whole G28 or SCAR-H replaces the insurer you do not have in Season (at +25% trader prices), whereas in PvP Zone Jaeger returns the rifle in 1-2 hours and in PvE an AI killer returns it with high probability.

Unavoidable in all three modes (required for both Provocation and Irresistible), so the question is only when to spend it: Season gains most because it is an outdoor container with no building entry on a Black-Division-free map and the guaranteed HighCom Trooper TFO spawn lands during Armor Shortage. Never burn one in the #11SR craft in Season — that craft also eats a non-renewable reader.

Multiple LEDX, an ophthalmoscope and a GPU behind one door is a slow deliberate search that PvE can afford on a local client; Season puts the same door on a Black Division roam map with no insurance on the escort kit, only partly offset by Handyman halving the Cultist Circle route (1x Mastichin figurine) that bypasses Ref LL3 entirely.

It cannot go in a secure container in any mode, so it is the one key whose loss is truly permanent — least irrational in PvE where the killer is AI, worst in Season where Streets is a Black Division roam map with no insurance behind it. Craftable at the Cultist Circle (1x Pointy guy figurine), so it is not find-in-raid-only.

Its documented max-uses field is blank where the three Reserve marked keys are capped at 25, and uncapped durability repays a permanent character far more than a 93-day one; PvE cannot claim a discount here because Streets forces BSG servers and the PvE flea is a separate, unreadable market.

Pure mobility, which is worth nothing against AI and negative in Season where Streets carries Black Division and no insurance; note a single key is guaranteed to spawn every raid behind the Brodion pub bar, so its flea restriction is irrelevant to acquiring it.

table.key: Health Resort east wing room 306 key
table.why_it_moves: Two rooms per unlock (306 chains to 308 via the balcony) is worth most where you can search both unhurried; the resort is the most contested building on Shoreline in both human modes and the map carries Black Division in Season. Acquire it via the Peacekeeper LL2 barter — the ₽5,780 infobox figure is a handbook base price with a blank trader field, not an offer.

table.key: Health Resort east wing room 328 key
table.why_it_moves: Same balcony-chain profile as 306 with a LEDX and a GPU; it moves only on how long you may stand in the east wing, which is why PvE ranks it and Season (Black Division roam plus uninsured escort gear) does not.

table.key: Health Resort west wing room 301 key
table.why_it_moves: The best loot-per-unlock on the map (301 plus 304 through the balcony: three GPU spawns, multiple LEDX, a 5x5 weapon box, an SV-98) with a free spawn on the yellow bus by the collapsed tunnel; Season holds a genuine counter-lever in Handyman converting that haul roughly twice as fast, which nearly offsets the Black Division risk.

A guaranteed Yellow keycard and two safes seconds from the eastern spawns; PvE gains from working both safes unhurried on a local client, and it stays usable in Season precisely because it is a short low-exposure stop far from the resort on a Black Division map.

A Therapist LL1 junk barter (Vita juice, milk, toilet paper) for a repeatable weapon-box door is disproportionately valuable on a fresh seasonal profile starting at LL1 with no insurance rebate, +25% trader prices and -20% sell payouts.

Barely moves once the false "only a permanent character banks Ref rep and GP coins" claim is dropped — Arena syncs one-way into Season too. Its one real mover is that PvE must flip the Interchange power switch itself every raid, which turns the power-station hideout into a free bolt-on to a detour you already pay for.

Same loot table in all three modes, so only cost differs: Reserve is not on the Season Black Division roam list, the key is mechanical so opt-in Safecracker stretches its 25 uses, and three used Reserve marked keys barter at Jaeger LL3 into a Dorm 314 key — a rouble-free path that never touches the flea.

Effectively mode-agnostic. Nothing stops you carrying all three Reserve marked keys in any mode (all are secure-container and Key tool storable, and the 5-per-raid cap is per key type), so the "triple circuit is PvE-only" premise does not hold.
Same as RB-BK; the underground tunnel geometry changes your approach in a human lobby but not the key's worth, and three extra drawers is not a meaningful stationary window.

The cheapest hideout barter (Ref LL1) for a guaranteed Yellow keycard, on a map Black Division do not roam in Season and which +25% seasonal XP reaches quickly; PvE gains the unhurried search. No lever isolates it for PvP Zone.

Free from the dead Scav's hand in the two-story dorm shower, and it opens twelve dorm key spawn locations plus a weapon rack and a 6x3 box — the bootstrap key in every mode, and it matters most in Season where you start at trader LL1 with no roubles and no insurance rebate.
